2608.10765.title: Compositional Benchmark Synthesis for Hierarchical Human Action Recognition
2608.10765.paper_summary: Recognizing human behavior across levels of abstraction, from atomic actions to long-horizon intentions, requires data annotated along a semantic hierarchy. Large corpora provide isolated, atomically labeled clips without temporal composition, whereas recorded composite-activity corpora offer shallow, domain-narrow, fixedhierarchies. A benchmark-generation and evaluation frameworkis proposed that synthesizes a four-level hierarchical-intention benchmark, spanning actions, activities, low-level intentions (LLIs), and high-level intentions (HLIs), from a flat single-label action corpus while retaining real pre-extracted features at the action level. Episodes are assembled by a transition model under a subject-consistency constraint, and a coverage-aware sampler reduces the subject usage Gini from 0.566 to 0.248. Synthesizing such a benchmark raises a circular-supervision risk that recorded datasets avoid: if the rules generating the episodes also govern the evaluation, models can succeed by recovering the generator rather than through genuine reasoning. Validity is addressed by design, holding sequence-generation rules disjoint from the first-order-logic rules used at evaluation. The instantiation yields 15,002 episodes. Four reference baselines from different model families characterize difficulty, not as recognition methods. A compositional held-out gap of 0.13 to 0.17 macro-F1 appears across all baselines, including a graph-aware model that recognizes best yet does not close the gap, indicating a structural property of the benchmark rather than a model artifact. A logic-free baseline still violates the held-out semantic rules above their intrinsic data rate, and the order-destroying control changes macro-F1 within seed variation, serving as a generator-consistency check. Theontology, transition model, and generator are released so the benchmark can beregenerated and extended.
2608.10765.paper_summary_zh: 辨識人類行為的抽象層次，從原子行動到長期意圖，需要沿著語義層次標註的數據。大型語料庫提供孤立的、原子標註的片段，缺乏時間組合，而錄製的複合活動語料庫則提供淺顯的、領域狹窄的固定層次。提出了一個基準生成和評估框架，該框架合成了一個四層級的意圖基準，涵蓋行動、活動、低層次意圖（LLIs）和高層次意圖（HLIs），從一個平坦的單標籤行動語料庫中提取，同時保留在行動層面的真實預提取特徵。根據主體一致性約束，通過轉換模型組裝集，並且一個考慮覆蓋率的抽樣器將主體使用的基尼指數從0.566降低到0.248。合成這樣的基準帶來了一個循環監督風險，而錄製的數據集則避免了這一點：如果生成集的規則也支配評估，模型可以通過恢復生成器而不是通過真正的推理來成功。有效性通過設計來解決，保持序列生成規則與用於評估的一階邏輯規則不相交。這一實例生成了15,002個集。來自不同模型家族的四個參考基準描述了難度，而不是作為識別方法。在所有基準中出現了0.13到0.17的組合性保留差距的宏觀F1，包括一個識別最佳但未能縮小差距的圖形感知模型，這表明基準的結構特性而非模型工件。一個無邏輯基準仍然違反了上述其內在數據率的保留語義規則，而破壞順序的控制在種子變異中改變了宏觀F1，作為生成器一致性的檢查。該本體、轉換模型和生成器已發布，以便基準可以被重新生成和擴展。
